dialogue.content: こんばんは
dialogue.English: Good evening.

dialogue.content: こんばんは、本日はよろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Good evening. Thank you for coming in today.

dialogue.content: こちらこそどうぞよろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Thank you for having me.

dialogue.content: こんばんは、相談員です。はじめに、年齢、性別を教えていただけますでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Good evening, I'm your counselor. To begin, could you please tell me your age and gender?

dialogue.content: はい、４５歳女性です。
dialogue.English: Yes, I'm a 45-year-old woman.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。本日はどのような相談内容になりますでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Thank you. What would you like to discuss today?

dialogue.content: そうですね・・・人に頼まれると断りにくい性格で、ちょっと色々やりすぎなこの頃です
dialogue.English: Well... I find it hard to say no when people ask me to do things, and lately I've been taking on a bit too much.

dialogue.content: 本当に嫌なことは断るのですが
dialogue.English: I do turn down things I really don't want to do, but...

dialogue.content: 好奇心もあって、ま、ちょっとやってみようかなと
dialogue.English: I'm also curious, so I tend to think, "Well, maybe I'll just give it a try."

dialogue.content: 手を出しすぎている状況は良くないなと感じています
dialogue.English: I feel that getting involved in too many things isn't good.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね。やり過ぎてしまうと、しんどいですよね。。。
dialogue.English: I see. It must be tough when you end up overdoing it...

dialogue.content: どんなことに手を出しているんですか？
dialogue.English: What kinds of things are you getting involved in?

dialogue.content: 今、PTAの役員になっています。
dialogue.English: Right now, I'm an officer on the PTA.

dialogue.content: それと、学校の改善要望を市に提出する活動とか
dialogue.English: Also, activities where we submit school improvement requests to the city,

dialogue.content: 防衛大学校人権侵害裁判の手伝いだとか
dialogue.English: and helping with the lawsuit regarding human rights violations at the National Defense Academy,

dialogue.content: 趣味の楽器の練習ができていません
dialogue.English: I haven't been able to practice my musical instrument, which is my hobby.

dialogue.content: なるほど、学校関連でいろいろやられているんですね。いろいろあると趣味とかの時間も削られてしまいますよね。。
dialogue.English: I see, so you're involved in various school-related activities. When you have so much going on, it does cut into your time for hobbies, doesn't it...

dialogue.content: はい。週３の仕事でもなれない役職で、色々勉強が必要です。
dialogue.English: Yes. Even at my three-days-a-week job, I'm in an unfamiliar position and have to study a lot.

dialogue.content: なるほど。。勉強も必要ですもんね。。学校関連はどのようにして始められたんですか？
dialogue.English: I see... Studying is necessary, too... How did you get started with the school-related activities?

dialogue.content: PTA役員は推薦ですね。
dialogue.English: I was nominated for the PTA officer role.

dialogue.content: 改善要望はNGO団体に所属しているので、そこでの活動です。
dialogue.English: The improvement requests are part of my activities with an NGO I belong to.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね。いろんな場所に所属してる感じなんですね。それはとても忙しい感じですね。。
dialogue.English: I see. It sounds like you're involved in several different groups. That must keep you very busy.

dialogue.content: PTAはもともと向いていないと思っていましたが、何事も経験かと思い引き受けました。２年の任期なのでもう一年頑張ってみますが自分には合わないなと思っています。
dialogue.English: I originally thought the PTA wasn't for me, but I accepted the role thinking it would be a good experience. It's a two-year term, so I'll try to stick it out for one more year, but I feel it's not a good fit for me.

dialogue.content: だからストレスに感じている状況です
dialogue.English: That's why I'm feeling stressed about it.

dialogue.content: 合ってないと思いながら頑張るとストレス溜まりますよね。耐えられているんですね。
dialogue.English: It must be stressful to keep pushing yourself when you feel it's not a good fit. You've been enduring it.

dialogue.content: そうですね。期間限定、修行だと思って。
dialogue.English: Yes. I see it as a limited-time training experience.

dialogue.content: ぐちを聞いてくれる同じ役員がいるのが救いです
dialogue.English: It's a relief that there's a fellow officer who listens to me vent.

dialogue.content: 愚痴を聞いてくれる人がいると、安心感がありますよね。修行ですか、ご自身の中で割り切られているところもある感じでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Having someone who will listen to you vent is reassuring, isn't it? You see it as training; does that mean you've come to terms with it in a way?

dialogue.content: えぇ、割り切って仕事してます。
dialogue.English: Yes, I'm compartmentalizing and just doing the work.

dialogue.content: 仲良しこよしでやるタイプではないので
dialogue.English: I'm not the type to do things in a chummy, buddy-buddy way.

dialogue.content: だから、PTAの役員LINEであまり関係のないやり取りが入るとちょっとイラッと来たりしてしまいますね
dialogue.English: So when unrelated chatter comes into the PTA officers' LINE group, I get a bit irritated.

dialogue.content: 関係ない話が入ると余計だと感じますよね。。実際に役員をやられてみてどうですか？
dialogue.English: It feels unnecessary when unrelated conversations come up, doesn't it? How has it been for you actually serving as an officer?

dialogue.content: そうですね・・・　学校の校長先生がちょっとパワハラちっくな人で、教頭先生へのその態度を見て嫌な気分になります。
dialogue.English: Well... the school principal is a bit of a bully, and it makes me feel bad to see how they treat the vice principal.

dialogue.content: あと、会長と合わないところがあって
dialogue.English: Also, there are aspects where I don't get along with the chairperson,

dialogue.content: それもイライラのもとです。
dialogue.English: and that's another source of frustration.

dialogue.content: うんうん、人を叱ってるところとか見てられないですよね。心痛めると言うか。。会長とはどの辺が合わないとお感じですか？
dialogue.English: Mmm-hmm, it's hard to watch someone being scolded, isn't it? It's heart-wrenching... In what ways do you feel you don't get along with the chairperson?

dialogue.content: 頑固な部分とか、ある方の仕事ですが進んでいないので、自分がちょっとやったのですが、そのことに感謝するより先に怒られたことで
dialogue.English: Their stubbornness, for one. And also, someone's work wasn't progressing, so I did a little bit of it, but instead of being thanked, I was scolded first.

dialogue.content: 私の中で会長に対してプチッと切れたところがあります。
dialogue.English: and that's when something in me just snapped a little toward the chairperson.

dialogue.content: 直接対決はしませんでしたが内心グラグラとしていました。
dialogue.English: I didn't confront them directly, but I was seething inside.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね、、、手伝ったことを怒られると切ない気持ちになりますよね。。。どうして、会長は怒られたんですか？
dialogue.English: I see... It's disheartening to be scolded for helping... Why did the chairperson scold you?

dialogue.content: その人の役割だから、その人がするべきだと。
dialogue.English: They said it was that person's role, so that person should do it.

dialogue.content: なるほど、役割を守れと。。。でも仕事の進みが遅かったわけですし、あんまりですよね。。。
dialogue.English: I see, "stick to your role"... But the work was falling behind, so that's a bit much...

dialogue.content: あなたの立場から間接的にどうなっているかを尋ねるようにして促してほしいと
dialogue.English: They wanted me to just indirectly ask how things were going from my position to nudge them along.

dialogue.content: ですね、結局、そのまましてたら遅くて、締切に間に合わない感じだったし。
dialogue.English: Right. But if I had left it as it was, it would have been too late, and we likely would have missed the deadline.

dialogue.content: 一度、やってくれてありがとう、でもね・・・
dialogue.English: I just wanted them to say, "Thank you for doing that, but..."

dialogue.content: と諭してほしかったんですよね
dialogue.English: ...and then explain it to me gently.

dialogue.content: そうですよね、ありがとうの一言ですよね。。ごまさんはとても良いことをしたと思いますよ！でも今回は相手が変だったと言うか合わなかったと言う感じですかね。。
dialogue.English: I agree, just a simple "thank you" was all that was needed. I think you did a very good thing! But in this case, it seems the other person was being unreasonable, or perhaps you two just weren't compatible.

dialogue.content: まぁ、そうなるんですかね。少し知り合いだったので、以前から抱いているイメージと違って「あれ？こんなに攻撃的な人だっけ？」
dialogue.English: Well, I guess so. I knew them a little, so it was different from the image I had of them. I thought, "Huh? Were they always this aggressive?"

dialogue.content: というギャップというか、戸惑いがありましたね。
dialogue.English: There was that gap, or rather, I was taken aback.

dialogue.content: がーっと言われると萎縮して、「もう意見あまり言いたくない。」ってなります。
dialogue.English: When someone comes at me hard, I shrink back and feel like, “I don't want to voice my opinions anymore.”

dialogue.content: そうでしたか、攻撃的に来られると驚きますよね。。言われて、我慢してしまった感じなんですね。。
dialogue.English: I see. It's startling when someone is aggressive towards you... It sounds like you were told off and just had to endure it.

dialogue.content: そうです。愚痴を聞いてくれる役員さんも言われたことがあるみたいで「（会長の指示がないから動いたのに）じゃあ私はどうすればいいの？」とはっきり伝えていました。
dialogue.English: That's right. The officer who listens to me vent seems to have been told off before too, and she clearly said to them, "(I acted because there were no instructions from you,) so what was I supposed to do?"

dialogue.content: なるほど、、言い返す人もいたんですね。。それを見てごまさんはどう感じましたか？
dialogue.English: I see, so there was someone who talked back... How did you feel when you saw that?

dialogue.content: お！よく言ったな。と思いました。結構溜め込むタイプの方が発言していたので、よっぽどだったと思います
dialogue.English: I thought, “Oh! Good for them.” They're the type to bottle things up, so it must have been really bad.

dialogue.content: 私は未だに言えないままですね。
dialogue.English: I still can't bring myself to say anything.

dialogue.content: 来年度は会長継続されないみたいなので我慢するかなと。
dialogue.English: It seems the chairperson won't continue next year, so I think I'll just put up with it.

dialogue.content: それは、よっぽどのことだったんですね。。ため込んだものが爆発した感じなんですね。。でも無理に言わないといけないということはないと思いますよ。
dialogue.English: That must have been quite something... Like something that had been building up just exploded... But I don't think you have to force yourself to speak up.

dialogue.content: 会長は継続なんですね。。
dialogue.English: So the chairperson is continuing, then...

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: 会長は継続なさそうです
dialogue.English: The chairperson doesn't seem to be continuing.

dialogue.content: なのであと４ヶ月くらいの辛抱です
dialogue.English: So I just have to put up with it for about four more months.

dialogue.content: なんとかなりそうです。
dialogue.English: I think I can manage.

dialogue.content: すみません、間違えました。ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: I'm sorry, I misunderstood. Thank you for correcting me.

dialogue.content: 校長先生も定年みたいですしね
dialogue.English: And the principal seems to be retiring, too.

dialogue.content: でも他の役職のかたの仕事にいろいろ口を出したくなります。
dialogue.English: But I find myself wanting to weigh in on the work of people in other positions.

dialogue.content: なるほどですね。環境が変わられていく感じなんですね。期間があると少しホッとするところがありますよね。
dialogue.English: I see. So the environment is going to change. It's a bit of a relief when there's an end in sight, isn't it?

dialogue.content: 例えば書記さんが議事録をデータでちゃんと残していないとか
dialogue.English: For example, the secretary isn't properly keeping a digital record of the minutes.

dialogue.content: うんうん
dialogue.English: Mmm-hmm.

dialogue.content: なんとなく議事録って残してないんですか？って聞いたらノートにありますって言われて。
dialogue.English: I casually asked, "Aren't you keeping the minutes?" and they said, "They're in a notebook."

dialogue.content: それだと閲覧しにくいですよね。。
dialogue.English: That makes them hard to access, doesn't it...

dialogue.content: パソコンが家にないらしく、それならノートをグループラインに写メってアップするでもいいのでって言ったけど
dialogue.English: Apparently, they don't have a computer at home, so I said it would be fine to just take a photo of the notebook and upload it to the group chat, but...

dialogue.content: 変わらないんですよ。
dialogue.English: nothing changes.

dialogue.content: そうなると、言い続けるのも疲れてしまいますもんね。。困ったものですよね。。
dialogue.English: When that happens, it gets tiring to keep saying it... It's a difficult situation...

dialogue.content: そうなんです。言うのもなんかためらわれるというか。言っても潰される感覚があって。議事録を残すことの大事さをわかってくれる役員もいるので孤立していないのが幸いです。
dialogue.English: Exactly. I hesitate to say anything, because it feels like my opinions will just be shot down. Fortunately, there are other officers who understand the importance of keeping minutes, so I'm not isolated.

dialogue.content: わかってくれる人がいるのが幸いですよね。。他の人は指摘とかはしないんですか？
dialogue.English: It's a relief that you have people who understand. Do the others not point it out?

dialogue.content: もう諦めているのか、議事録賛成派は書記に断っているのかわかりませんが、議事録勝手に作ってますね。
dialogue.English: I'm not sure if they've given up or if they've already told the secretary, but the pro-minutes faction is making the minutes themselves now.

dialogue.content: それは二度手間で本来の人の意味がなくなってしまいますよね。。なかなか状況的に複雑な感じなんですね。。。
dialogue.English: That's double the work and defeats the purpose of having that person in the role... It sounds like a rather complicated situation...

dialogue.content: 会長はその人には書記の仕事でしょ！と私のときのように叱ったりしていないような感じがします。
dialogue.English: It feels like the chairperson isn't scolding that person the way they scolded me, saying "That's the secretary's job!"

dialogue.content: もう、できる人が、やれる人が、できるときにやったらいいじゃないと思う自分と
dialogue.English: Part of me thinks, “The people who are capable should just do what they can, when they can,”

dialogue.content: 役割を与えられた人がやらないと、その人が成長しないでしょ派の会長では、すれ違いなんでしょうね。
dialogue.English: but that clashes with the chairperson, who's in the "If the person assigned the role doesn't do it, they won't grow" camp. I guess we're just not on the same page.

dialogue.content: それは不公平感があり、納得できないですよね。意見がすれ違うと虚しくなりますよね。。なかなかうまく回らない状況なんですね。。。
dialogue.English: That feels unfair and is hard to accept. It's disheartening when your opinions clash... It seems things aren't running very smoothly...

dialogue.content: 能力の差とか、仕事が立て込んでいて忙しいためにできない人もいるのになと。PTAは仕事じゃないし。あくまでボランティアでやっているんだからなぁって。
dialogue.English: I think about how some people can't do things because of differences in ability, or because they're swamped with their actual jobs. The PTA isn't a job. We're just doing this as volunteers, after all.

dialogue.content: おっしゃるようにすれ違いで虚しくなってしまうことはありますね
dialogue.English: As you say, it does feel disheartening when we're at odds like this.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。ボランティアというところがミソですよね。皆でよくしたいと気持ちでやってるからこそ、虚しさを感じますよね。。
dialogue.English: Right. The fact that it's volunteer work is the key point. You feel that emptiness precisely because everyone is supposed to be doing it with the intention of making things better together.

dialogue.content: 虚しさを感じると活動を楽しめないです。
dialogue.English: When I feel that emptiness, I can't enjoy the activities.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。。やるなら楽しみたいのですよね。。今仰ったことをまとめてもよろしいですか？
dialogue.English: I understand... If you're going to do it, you want to enjoy it... Would it be all right if I summarize what you've just told me?

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: ごまさんはPTA役員NGO団体で慣れない状況の中活動されている。仕事に対しては真摯で不要なやりとりとかは余計と感じる時がありその中で自分の意見を我慢してしまうところにストレスを感じる。PTAに関しては、会長の意見と合わず、会長はできなくとも役割を持つべき人がやるべきと思っている。ただ、仕事が回らなくなっており、できる人（ごまさん）がやり、手伝ったことに対して怒られる事態になる。現場ですれ違いが発生しており、虚しい状況。残り4ヶ月で会長は退くが、残りの4ヶ月が不安。
dialogue.English: You're active as a PTA officer and in an NGO in unfamiliar situations. You're sincere about the work and sometimes feel that unnecessary interactions are a waste of time, which causes stress as you hold back your opinions. Regarding the PTA, you don't agree with the chairperson, who believes the person assigned a role should do it, even if they're unable to. However, the work isn't getting done, so a capable person like you steps in, only to be scolded for helping. There's a clash happening, which creates a disheartening situation. The chairperson will be leaving in four months, but you're anxious about those remaining four months.

dialogue.content: いかがでしょうか？
dialogue.English: How does that sound?

dialogue.content: 学校の状況はあってます。NGO団体では言いたいことが言えて、割とやりたいことができる環境でそこそこ楽しんでいますが、色々頼まれすぎているなと感じます。残りの４ヶ月に不安は、そこまでないですね。
dialogue.English: The school situation is correct. At the NGO, I can say what I want to say, and it's an environment where I can pretty much do what I want, so I enjoy it to some extent. However, I do feel I'm being asked to do too much. I'm not that anxious about the remaining four months, though.

dialogue.content: 色々頼まれすぎて抱え込みすぎるのが悩みですかね
dialogue.English: I guess my main problem is being asked to do too much and taking on more than I can handle.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you for clarifying.

dialogue.content: やれないことはないと思ってしまう。なんとかやってしまうため、また頼まれる。
dialogue.English: I tend to think that nothing is impossible. And because I somehow manage to get it done, I get asked again.

dialogue.content: 人から頼まれるのは、急には止まらないですもんね。。でもこのままパンクしても嫌ですもんね。
dialogue.English: The requests from others won't just suddenly stop, will they... But you don't want to burn out either.

dialogue.content: そのとおりです
dialogue.English: Exactly.

dialogue.content: ごまさんの中で理想はどのような形を描いてますか？
dialogue.English: In your mind, what would be the ideal situation?

dialogue.content: う～ん
dialogue.English: Hmm...

dialogue.content: 何を軸にするかなぁと思ったときにこれと決められないんですよ
dialogue.English: When I think about what to make my priority, I can't decide on just one thing.

dialogue.content: ただ、世のため、人のため、弱者のために
dialogue.English: But, for the good of society, for others, for the vulnerable...

dialogue.content: みたいな思いはずっとありますね。
dialogue.English: I've always had that kind of feeling.

dialogue.content: このカウンセラーの勉強もその一つです
dialogue.English: Studying to be a counselor is one part of that.

dialogue.content: 決断は難しいですよねご自身の中で志を持っておられるのはとても良いことですよね。
dialogue.English: Making a decision is difficult, isn't it? It's a wonderful thing that you have such aspirations.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: だとしたら、ご自身の依頼を受け付けるのを 、志のハードルを超えるもの以外に関しては、
dialogue.English: In that case, when it comes to accepting requests, for anything that doesn't clear the high bar of your aspirations,

dialogue.content: 引き受けるのではなく、その場で相手にアドバイスする形で完了させるのはいかがですかね？
dialogue.English: how about instead of taking them on, you wrap things up by giving the person advice on the spot?

dialogue.content: ほほぉ。
dialogue.English: Oh, interesting.

dialogue.content: 自分は動かなくていいですものね。
dialogue.English: That way, I don't have to do the work myself.

dialogue.content: つっぱねるとご自身が苦しくなるし、引き受けると仕事が増えるので、上記対応というのも一つ選択肢としてはアリかもしれないですよね。
dialogue.English: Flatly refusing might make you feel bad, and accepting increases your workload, so the approach I just mentioned could be a viable option.

dialogue.content: うん、うん。　ネックなのはマンパワーがなく、やらざるを得ない状況が多いことなんですよね・・・
dialogue.English: Yes, yes. The sticking point is that we often lack the manpower, so we end up in situations where someone just has to do it...

dialogue.content: でも、今後のために、その選択肢は持っておこうと思いました。
dialogue.English: But for the future, I think I'll keep that option in mind.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: それは良かったです。でやらざる得ないという状況になる前から、きっちり動ければ苦労はしないですもんね。。。
dialogue.English: I'm glad. If things could be handled properly before reaching the point where you have to step in, it wouldn't be so troublesome...

dialogue.content: ですね
dialogue.English: Right.

dialogue.content: 頑張りすぎないことに対して応援してます。時間を見つけて趣味にも使える時間が増えると良いですよね！
dialogue.English: I'm cheering you on in not overdoing it. I hope you can find more time for your hobbies.

dialogue.content: 混乱期を少しずつ整備していく運命なのかしらと考えるようにしています。あと１年なので今より開けるようにしたいです。
dialogue.English: I'm trying to think of it as my destiny to gradually bring order to this chaotic period. I have one more year, so I'd like to have more breathing room than I do now.

dialogue.content: 運命と割り切ることは大事ですよね。
dialogue.English: Accepting it as destiny is important, isn't it?

dialogue.content: 根は楽天的なんだと思います。来年こそは今よりも趣味の時間を持つことを目標にぼちぼちやっていきますね。
dialogue.English: I think I'm an optimist at heart. I'll make it my goal to have more time for my hobbies next year and just take things at my own pace.

dialogue.content: 良い感じですね！応援してます！それでは、本日の相談を終了させて頂きます。
dialogue.English: That sounds wonderful! I'm rooting for you! With that, we'll conclude today's session.

dialogue.content: また、よろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: I look forward to our next session.

dialogue.content: はい、ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Yes, thank you very much.
